questions.question: A 640 metre long train travelling at 80 km/h overtook a 540 metre long train travelling at 72 km/h in the same direction. How long did it take the faster train to cross the other train completely?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 80 − 72 = 8 km/h

Relative speed in m/s = 8 × 5/18 = 20/9 m/s

Total distance to cover = 640 + 540 = 1180 m

Time = 1180 ÷ (20/9) = 59 × 9 = 531 seconds

531 seconds = 8 minutes 51 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 8 minutes 51 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of faster train (L₁) = 640 m

Length of slower train (L₂) = 540 m

Speed of faster train (S₁) = 80 km/h

Speed of slower train (S₂) = 72 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 
• 
 
 Train 1: 640m
 
 Train 2: 540m
 

 S1 = 80 km/h
 

 S2 = 72 km/h
 Relative Speed = S1 − S2 (Same Direction)
 Total Distance = 640 + 540 = 1180 m

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance to be covered = L₁ + L₂ = 640 + 540 = 1180 m

⇒ Relative speed = 80 − 72 = 8 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 8 × (5/18) = 40/18 = 20/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken = 1180 ÷ (20/9)

⇒ Time taken = 1180 × 9/20

⇒ Time taken = 59 × 9 = 531 seconds

⇒ Time in minutes = 531 ÷ 60 = 8 minutes and 51 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 8 minutes 51 seconds.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concepts

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their speeds. When they move in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Distance

When a train crosses another train, a bridge, or a platform, the total distance covered is the sum of the lengths of the two objects.</p

questions.question:
A dice is thrown 150 times, with the frequencies for the outcomes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 being as given in the following table. How many times is the number appearing on the dice a prime number?

 
 

 Outcome
 1
 2
 3
 4
 5
 6
 
 

 Frequency
 23
 43
 33
 13
 10
 28
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify prime numbers on a dice: 2, 3, and 5.

Sum their corresponding frequencies from the table.

Total frequency of prime numbers = 43 + 33 + 10 = 86.

**∴ The correct answer is 86.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given Data from Frequency Table:

Frequency of Outcome 1 = 23

Frequency of Outcome 2 = 43

Frequency of Outcome 3 = 33

Frequency of Outcome 4 = 13

Frequency of Outcome 5 = 10

Frequency of Outcome 6 = 28

Total Throws = 150

Prime numbers in the set {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}:

⇒ 1 is neither prime nor composite.

⇒ 2 is a prime number.

⇒ 3 is a prime number.

⇒ 4 is a composite number (2 × 2).

⇒ 5 is a prime number.

⇒ 6 is a composite number (2 × 3).

Calculation for prime number frequency:

⇒ Total prime frequency = Freq(2) + Freq(3) + Freq(5)

⇒ Total prime frequency = 43 + 33 + 10

⇒ Total prime frequency = 86

**∴ The correct answer is 86.**

**__Additional Information__**

Definition of Prime Numbers

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself. The first few are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11...

Special Case of 1

The number 1 is not considered a prime number because it does not have exactly two distinct divisors; it only has one divisor (1).

Probability of Prime Numbers

The experimental probability P(Prime) = (Total frequency of prime outcomes) ÷ (Total number of trials). In this case, P(Prime) = 86 ÷ 150 = 43/75.</p

questions.question: Sudhir claimed to sell his items at only 8% above the cost of production, but used a weight that had 750 grams written on it, though it actually weighed 720 grams. What was the actual profit percentage earned by Sudhir?
questions.solution:
**FORMULA USED:**

Profit = S.P. - C.P.

Profit% = (Profit/C.P.) × 100

Where, S.P = Selling price, C.P. = Cost price 

**CALCULATION:**

Sudhir sells his items at an 8% profit 

⇒ Profit% =( Profit /C.P.) × 100

⇒ 8 = (S.P. - C.P.)/C.P. × 100 

⇒ 108 C.P. = 100 S.P. or S.P.= 1.08 C.P.

But when Sudhir uses weights that measure only 720 grams while he claims to measure 750 grams

Hence, C.P. of 720 grams = (720/750) × Original C.P. = 0.96 of original C.P.

So, he is selling goods worth 0.96 at 1.08 C.P. 

⇒ Hence, he makes a profit of ( 1.08 - 0.96) = 0.12 C.P. on his cost of 0.96 C.P.

⇒ Profit% = ( 0.12/ 0.96) × 100 = 12.5

**Hence, actual Profit percentage earned by Sudhir is 12.5%.**

The volume of the cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

Here, Length = 12m , Breadth = 6m , Height = 0.5 m

⇒ Volume = Length × Breadth × Height = 12 × 6 × 0.5 = **36 m3**

**Hence, the required Volume is 36 m³****.**

questions.question: A can complete a work in 5 days and B can complete the same work in 10 days. If A and B work alternately, starting with A, in how many days will they complete the work?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

A completes the work = 5 days

B completes the work = 10 days

A and B work alternately

**CALCULATION:**

Complete the work in 5 days

⇒ A's 1 day work = 1/5 

B complete the work in 10 days

⇒ B's 1 day work = 1/10

⇒ ( A + B )'s work in 2 days = ( 1/5 + 1/10)= 3/10 

In 3 pairs of 2 days they will complete 3/10 × 3 = 9/10

⇒ Hence, after 3 × 2 = 6 days, 1 - 9/10 = 1/10 work is left which will be done by A alone.

⇒ A does 1 work in 5 days 

⇒ A does 1/10 work in 5 × 1/10 = 1/2 days

⇒ Total number of days = 6 + 1/2 = 6 1over 2days

**Hence, they will complete the work in 6 1over 2 days.**

questions.question: A merchant gives an additional discount of 10% on the product after an initial discount of 20% on the listed price. He managed to make a 10% profit by selling the product for ₹54,000. What was the listed price of the product?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Initial discount = 20%

additional discount = 10%

Selling price = Rs54000

**FORMULA USED:**

S.P. = ( 1-d1/100) × ( 1-d2/100) × M.P.

Where, S.P. = Selling price 

M.P. = Marked price or listed price

d1 and d2 are successive discounts respectively

**CALCULATION:**

Here S.P. = Rs54000 , d1 = 20% and d2 = 10%

⇒ S.P. = ( 1- d1/100) × ( 1- d2/100) × M.P.

⇒ 54000 = ( 1 - 20/100 ) × ( 1- 10/100) × M.P.

⇒ 54000 = ( 1-1/5) × ( 1- 1/10) × M.P.

⇒ 54000 = 4/5 × 9/10 × M.P.

⇒ M.P. = Rs75,000

**Hence, the Marked price of the listed price is Rs75,000.**
